decisive_items: She had been applying this ointment to her face at least daily for 2 years, pausing for no more than 1–2 days at a time because the rash promptly returned.
She stopped the ointment completely 3 days before presentation.
studded with numerous 2– to 3-mm pustules, some coalescing into “lakes of pus.”
response.rationale: Chronic topical steroid use with rebound after cessation and periorificial pustular “lakes of pus” are classic for steroid-induced rosacea-like dermatitis; perioral dermatitis is less specific and topical steroid withdrawal lacks this pustular morphology.

rejected.why: Topical steroid withdrawal alone does not explain the pustular “lakes of pus” or the periorificial distribution; the morphology and steroid-rebound timing favor steroid-induced rosacea-like dermatitis.
